artists.biography:
Rancid is an American punk rock band formed in Berkeley, California in 1991. Founded by 80s punk veterans Tim Armstrong and Matt Freeman, both of whom previously played in the highly influential ska punk band Operation Ivy, Rancid is credited—along with Green Day and The Offspring—for reviving mainstream interest in punk rock in the United States during the mid-1990s. Unlike Green Day and The Offspring however, Rancid remained signed to an independent record label and retained much of its original fan-base, most of which was connected to its underground roots.

Rancid includes Tim Armstrong on guitar and vocals, Freeman on bass and vocals, Lars Frederiksen on guitar and vocals, and Branden Steineckert on drums. The band was formed by Armstrong, Freeman, and former drummer Brett Reed, who left the band in 2006 and was replaced by Steineckert. Frederiksen joined Rancid in 1993 when the band was searching for a second guitar player.

To date, Rancid has released seven studio albums, one split album, one compilation, two extended plays, and a series of live online-only albums, and has been featured on a number of compilation albums. The band has independently sold over four million records worldwide, making it one of the most successful independent punk groups of all time. The band rose to fame in 1994 with its second studio album, Let's Go, featuring the single "Salvation". In the following year, Rancid released its highly successful album ...And Out Come the Wolves, which produced its best-known songs "Roots Radicals", "Ruby Soho" and "Time Bomb", and was certified gold and platinum by the RIAA, selling over one million copies in the United States alone. Its next four albums, Life Won't Wait, Rancid, Indestructible and Let the Dominoes Fall, were also critically acclaimed, though not as successful as ...And Out Come the Wolves. Rancid is currently recording an eighth studio album, which is expected to be released in 2013.

...And Out Come The Wolves, released in 1995 on Epitaph Records, is Rancid's third studio album and a landmark in 1990s punk rock. The album showcases a dynamic blend of punk rock, ska, and pop influences, reflecting the band's roots and evolution. It features a range of styles from aggressive punk tracks like "Maxwell Murder," highlighted by Matt Freeman's intense bass solo, to the catchy, melodic "Ruby Soho," and the ska-punk hybrid "Time Bomb," a sound pioneered by band members Tim Armstrong and Matt Freeman in their earlier band Operation Ivy.

This album solidified Rancid's place in punk rock history, capturing the mid-1990s punk revival and expanding their audience beyond underground circles. Produced by Jerry Finn and mixed by Andy Wallace, ...And Out Come The Wolves received critical acclaim for its concise songwriting and authentic portrayal of street life and personal struggles. The album's title references a poem from Jim Carroll's Basketball Diaries, underscoring its cultural resonance within punk rock.

Commercially and critically, the album was a breakthrough for Rancid, with singles like "Time Bomb" and "Ruby Soho" gaining significant radio airplay and enduring popularity. It remains one of the most influential punk albums of its era, often cited for its lasting impact on the genre and its role in defining the sound of 1990s punk rock.
